claims: A focused self-test can pass inside a real gate run: `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:601` — the guard only refuses `GATE_TEST_FOCUS` when `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` or `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set, but with `--no-lock` the lock step returns early (`:1616`) and never sets `LOCK_HELD`, so a focus exported in the developer's shell reaches the mapped `pnpm agent:quality-gate:test`

A green focused no-lock run with no reuse writes `last-success.stamp` (`agent-quality-gate.sh:5868-5878`), which doesn't cover environment variables, so the pre-push hook's `--skip-if-fresh` then skips every mapped command (`:4843-4848`) until the stamp expires

Stale text: the comment at `test.sh:595-597` and the doc at `agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1143-1145` both say `LOCK_HELD` is on "any command a real gate run spawns", which isn't true for no-lock runs
Nothing tests the new guards: `test.sh:600-605` — no test would fail if the focus refusal were deleted; no test covers the gate's different run modes
The verifier's failure branches aren't tested either (`test.sh:473-575`)

The abort message reports the wrong line on macOS's built-in bash 3.2: `test.sh:21-24` — `$LINENO` inside a function's error trap gives the function's opening line, so every abort would say `line <run_X_family() {>` instead of the line that failed

judge_reasoning.3829986398: Review's trap finding is about $LINENO reporting the wrong line on bash 3.2, not about an unset output_file under set -u.
judge_reasoning.3829986403: Review never flags that multiple dispatch_gate_test_families calls pass validation; it only says the verifier rejects stray lines.
judge_reasoning.3830003055: Review does not mention that a missing dispatch call passes the partition check and silently exits 0.
judge_reasoning.3830042123: Review finding 1 identifies that the focus guard is bypassed in --no-lock / AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0 runs because LOCK_HELD is never exported.
judge_reasoning.3830042128: Review does not mention the hard-coded self-test path pin missing from the path-pin inventory.
judge_reasoning.3830695396: Review flags the doc text as stale about LOCK_HELD coverage in no-lock runs, not the 'is set' vs 'non-empty' / 'reds' wording issue.

1.why: Checked it: acquire_gate_run_lock returns early at agent-quality-gate.sh:1616 when --no-lock is set, before LOCK_HELD is exported at :1143, so the guard at test.sh:601 lets a focus through. This is the known 'Reject focus during lock-free gate runs' defect.

2.why: Checked it: stamp_line (:4764) hashes only base, paths, plan, implementation, content and package-risk, with no env, and :5868-5878 writes the stamp on a green no-reuse run. But this is just the downstream effect of the known lock-free focus leak, not a separate defect.

3.why: The comment at test.sh:595-597 and the doc at mechanics.md:1143-1145 do say LOCK_HELD is on 'every/any command a real gate run spawns', which is false for --no-lock. It is the same lock-free gap, and it overlaps the known doc item.

4.why: git grep finds GATE_TEST_FOCUS only in the dispatch itself and the doc. No test runs the dispatch with a focus plus LOCK_HELD, GITHUB_ACTIONS or --no-lock, so deleting the refusal at :600-605 would not fail any test.

5.why: verify_gate_family_partition (:485-574) only ever runs against the real, well-formed file. No fixture exercises fail_partition, the awk error branches or the registry-order diff, so a broken verifier would go unnoticed.

6.why: Reproduced it: under /bin/bash 3.2.57, an ERR trap re-armed inside a function reports the function's opening line (line 7), while bash 5.3 reports the failing line (line 11). The repo's Bash floor is 3.2 (mechanics.md:196), and before this change the tests ran at top level, so this is a regression.
